text:
sara: heads-up — after the driver bump to 545.12 on canary we started seeing a sharp drop in KV-prefetch/autotune hit rate and a 95th increase on small-seq paths. profiler dump attached: s3://redwood-telemetry/canary/2234567890/kv-autotune.pfl

mike: saw the same on our latency dashboards. 95th for 8-16 tokens jumped ~30ms around the deploy window. correlates with more requests falling into the slow kernel path. :frowning:

anya: i pulled a flamegraph — looks like kernel selector is choosing the legacy conv-attn path for many h100 jobs that used optimized tensorop before. attaching snippet:
```
selector.log:
seq_len=12 gpu=h100 arch=sm90 candidate_kernels=[tensorop_fast, conv_attn, fallback] 
chosen=conv_attn reason=tie_break_global_cost
```

jon: is the autotuner's cost model using driver-reported flop timings? recent driver changes can affect kernel timing numbers used by the ranker.

mike: yes, autotuner uses the kernel latency table that we populate from microbenchmarks. driver math changed some kernels' fp timings and the heuristic re-weighted conv_attn higher.

sara: deploy-bot, what rolled when?

deploy-bot: rolled: runtime:canary -> 2026-03-08T02:14Z by infra/canary-rolling. image: runtime:v0.58.2, cuda-driver:545.12

anya: quick mitigation ideas: 1) force kernel blacklist for conv_attn on affected seqlens/gpus, 2) tweak tie-breaker to prefer lower-latency kernel by sampled online timings, 3) rollback driver on canary.

jon: i can sketch a temporary blacklist rule. but we should avoid long-lived hard blacklists. can we do an online re-score using percentile latencies from real requests?

mike: we already have a telemetry pipeline that samples 0.5% of requests and stores per-kernel med/95 latency in tsdb. we can fold that into the autotuner and bias selections. problem: the new driver changed baseline so the offline microbenchmarks are stale.

sara: action items => mike will backfill the sampled real-request kernel latencies for the last 3 hours and run a quick re-score, anya will craft a temporary kernel blacklist rule for seq_len<=16 on h100, jon will prepare rollback steps and a staging canary to validate, i'll coordinate ops.

mike: backfill command i'm running now: 
```
python infra/tools/telemetry_agg.py --from=2234567000 --to=2234567900 --metrics=kernel_latency_percentiles --filter=gpu=h100,seq_len<=16 --out=/tmp/kv_realtime_rank.json
```

anya: blacklist patch (hotfix) i'm proposing:
```json
{ "rule": "if gpu.arch==\"sm90\" and seq_len<=16 then deprioritize conv_attn by +20ms" }
```
will open PR to canary ruleset.

jon: rollback plan: we can revert driver on canary pool to 542.x images, test perf with loadgen for 10k requests across seq distribution, then promote. ETA ~45m if infra gives 👍. i'll post the validation checklist.

mike: initial backfill shows conv_attn 95p increased from 6ms -> 36ms for seq_len<=12 after the bump. tensorop_fast remains ~5-7ms. re-scoring would flip many picks back.

sara: ok — two-pronged: push anya's hotfix blacklist to canary ruleset immediately (low blast), start rollback validation in parallel, and trigger autotuner to ingest sampled latencies so we can do a safer automatic reweight. i'll create a ticket and tag sla/ops.

anya: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/11234 — hotfix rule + test. cc @mike for telemetry integration tests. :eyes:

mike: once PR merges i'll run a gated canary apply. after rule is applied, we should see 95p drop back in ~2-3 minutes due to in-flight evictions.

deploy-bot: runtime canary ruleset updated by infra/canary-apply at 2026-03-08T02:57Z

jon: rollback dry-run completed in staging, no functional regressions. starting driver revert on 10% of canary nodes now.

sara: keep logs of kernel_selector decisions for the reverted nodes so we can compare. tag logs with canary-node-id.

mike: after blacklist applied + partial rollback, 95p for seq<=16 fell from +30ms anomaly to +3ms. autotuner ingestion job queued.

anya: follow-up: we need a durable fix — either update microbenchmark suite to include the new driver behavior and recompute kernel latency tables, or add an online weighted estimator into autotuner. my vote: both.

sara: agreed. i'll schedule a short post-mortem and a follow-up ticket to add online estimator and expand microbench coverage to capture driver dependent FP kernel timing changes. thanks all. :thumbsup:
